name: Ashveil Ironmark Gang Colors Vest
description:
A sleeveless denim-analog vest in oxidized indigo, stiffened with resin-soaked salvage cloth backing. Hand-painted territorial sigils cover the rear panel — layered over years, each mark a palimpsest of alliances and victories. Chest patches are heat-bonded corponation logo inversions, deliberately defaced. Sleeve holes are raw-cut and re-hemmed with copper wire stitching.

Color saturation and patch density signal rank within the crew. A bare back means prospect. A fully covered back means you've bled for this block.
functionality: Reinforced rear panel provides minor impact absorption. Copper wire hem conducts static discharge in acid-rain conditions. Hidden interior pocket sewn beneath the left chest panel.
what_it_says: This person belongs to a specific block, has history with it, and will defend it.
story_hooks: A runner finds this vest on a body — the sigils match a crew that officially dissolved six years ago.
A Tier 3 fashion blogger is caught wearing a bootleg version; the original crew sends a message.
The vest's layered paint conceals a hand-drawn map of Shelf tunnel routes beneath the topmost sigil.

physical_description.visual_profile: A weathered, defiant sleeveless vest that reads as street armor. The oxidized indigo creates a faded, almost ghostly blue-grey tone. Layered paint and patches create visual density across the back, telling a narrative of territorial claims and crew history. The silhouette is deliberately utilitarian—broad shoulders, straight lines, no vanity.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, slightly oversized through the torso to accommodate layered clothing underneath. Cut short to mid-torso, exposing the wearer's sides. Armholes are deliberately crude and wide, suggesting rapid alteration rather than tailoring.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy denim-analog (synthetic cotton-polyester blend, likely salvaged or low-tier manufactured). Backing layer is resin-stiffened recycled textile composite, creating structural rigidity and weight.
physical_description.texture: Rough and granular where resin-treatment has set unevenly. Paint layers create a matte, chalk-like surface over the hand-applied sigils. Raw denim edges are frayed and soft. Copper wire stitching is cold and tactile—intentionally visible.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant oxidized indigo (faded, desaturated blue-grey). Overlaid hand-painted sigils in acrylic or crude pigments—blacks, blood-reds, silvers, and occasional fluorescent accents (illegal corp-drain dyes). Defaced logo inversions appear as reverse-printed patches or paint-over distortions in whites and dark greys.
physical_description.closures: None. Pulled over the head. The raw-cut armholes and lack of buttons or zippers reinforce the 'ripped from salvage' aesthetic.
distinctive_features: Rear panel completely covered in hand-painted territorial sigils—layered over years, creating palimpsest effect
Chest patches featuring inverted/defaced corponation logos—heat-bonded then deliberately vandalized
Copper wire stitching replacing traditional seams at armholes—visible and intentional
Resin-soaked backing creating visible stiffness and weight
Raw-cut, re-hemmed edges throughout—no finished seams
Visible wear and aging—fading follows stress points, creating authentic degradation patterns
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 / Sub-Grade. Hand-made crew gear signals no corporate affiliation. The deliberately defaced logos and salvage construction mark this as street-level, ungoverned territory.
physical_description.cultural_context: Gang colors. Ashveil Ironmark crew member. A walking claim of territorial dominance and crew loyalty. Wearing this vest is a declaration—you belong to this block, this crew, this history. Paint density signals rank and experience; a bare back means prospect status; full coverage means blood-earned standing.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn and weathered. Edges are frayed from use, not by design. Resin may be flaking in places. Paint layers show uneven aging—some sigils sharp and fresh, others faded and cracked. Copper stitching may show green patina or small breaks. The vest should look *used*, not manufactured.

image_prompt: Close-up fashion photography of a weathered indigo denim-analog sleeveless vest displayed on a dark chrome mannequin, three-quarter view showing layered hand-painted territorial sigils across the back panel. Paint marks in black, deep red, and silver create a palimpsest narrative. Defaced corponation logo patches visible on chest. Copper wire stitching gleams at raw armholes. Resin-stiffened texture visible in harsh, angled studio lighting casting deep shadows. Urban cyberpunk backdrop with rain-slicked pavement and neon signs reflecting off wet concrete. Gritty, high-contrast color grading emphasizing oxidized indigo and paint layers. Moody, gang-affiliated street aesthetic. --ar 2:3 --v 6
